record_reviews.summary: Hooker writes on 6 April and adds a separate 7 April Calcutta section. He discusses Darwin’s health and species/barnacle work, says Sikkim did not clarify Darwin’s doctrines, develops a new double-chain/glacial interpretation of the Himalaya, and then reports Falconer’s delayed letters and his own arrival in Calcutta.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Two recorded dates, 6 and 7 Apr 1850, with order held. P1-P6 are the first section; P7-P8 are explicitly headed 7 April and change to Calcutta/Falconer matters.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker’s prose is complete; CD annotations and the editorial footnote about Darwin’s notes are separate.

evidence.quote: I received your kind & full letters 2 months ago & deeply I sympathize with your wifes & your own pleasure in knowing your health to be really improving
I hope that there cannot be a shadow of a doubt, that long before this letter gets to India, you will be a free man.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin acknowledges a recent Hooker letter, responds to the stratification/foliation argument with gneiss and inversion observations, praises Hooker’s Galapagos and Antarctic writing, discusses his water treatment and fossil cirripede publication, then reacts to Falconer’s neglect and Malcolmson’s death.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially 13 June [1850]. Footnote says the opening comments refer to Hooker’s 30 September 1849 letter 1257, while P6’s Falconer paragraph plausibly engages 1319; preserve both layers.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s seven paragraphs are complete; the editorial cross-reference is not a reason to collapse the letter to one antecedent.

evidence.quote: I never heard anything so strange as Falconer’s neglect of your letters: I am extremely glad you are cordial with him again
he played me another sad trick since last mid summer keeping all my letters & overland parcels for 5 months

record_reviews.summary: Hooker reports months of Falconer failing to forward letters and parcels, travels from Khasi/Jyntea toward Munnipore and Chittagong, compares Himalayan and Asian mountain chains, discusses denudation, coal roots, botany at tropical elevations, and hopes to see Darwin before returning home.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 26 Nov 1850; the body is one dated letter with no internal section date.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker’s 20 paragraphs are complete; named correspondents and published reports are reported sources.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No explicit Darwin prompt is identified; Falconer correspondence problems and geological reflections are Hooker’s own account.

record_reviews.summary: Hooker reads Darwin’s Geology of South America at high altitude, distinguishes stratification, foliation and cleavage, reports Himalayan gneiss, glaciers and terraces, and critiques Darwin’s Admiralty instructions for omitting prices of instruments and books.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Hooker’s 12 paragraphs are complete; CD’s marginal annotations are separate.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Context previously read in batch05; no duplicate relation.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin answers Hooker’s geological report, comparing Himalayan terraces with Chile, arguing that the Yangma dam is a lateral moraine, discussing glacial scoring and the failed Tibet crossing, then adding Birmingham, water-cure and species-work news.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s ten paragraphs are complete; Sabine, Ross and Athenæum references are reported external material.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: Context previously read in batch05; no duplicate relation.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin worries about Hooker’s reported imprisonment, explains that Henslow obtained details through Hooker’s father, reports fossil cirripede work, the birth of Leonard, concern about Falconer and the Fitton shipwreck.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Editorially 3 Feb [1850]; the body gives no alternate internal day.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s six paragraphs are complete; imprisonment news comes from newspapers/family correspondence.
record_reviews.unmatched_reason: No specific incoming Hooker prompt survives.

proposed_links.reason: Hooker says he received Darwin’s “kind & full letters 2 months ago” and responds to Darwin’s improving health and family/species concerns. The 3 February 1300 letter is a plausible component, but the plural “letters” and two-month approximation do not establish it as the sole antecedent or an exact receipt date.
proposed_links.response_scope: 1319 P1-P3, broad health/species response; P4-P6 are Hooker’s new Himalayan interpretation.
